title: Choose the visual world
question: Re-roll: the roll assigned The Drawing Set. Keep it, take an alternate, or re-roll.

options.label: The Drawing Set
options.lineage: architectural construction drawing sets and their title blocks
options.thesis: The portfolio is a set of drawing sheets: each section is a sheet, and a title block in the corner always carries name and contact.
options.viewport: Sheet A-001: NAVIN set huge on a white sheet framed by a hairline border; a title block in the lower right holds role, school, the race and email actions; the portrait sits as a framed elevation; the sheet index along the top shows the scroll position.
options.risk: Dimension lines and grids can become decoration; every line must label or measure something real.

raised.raise: One identical sheet frame repeats on every section, so the frame itself becomes the ruler you read the site by.
Every record carries its spec beside it (year, role, stack); no item stands without its data.
The next sheet announces itself: the index ahead brightens as you approach, the past greys out.
Each sheet has one loudest fragment, the eye's single entry point, and everything else steps down.
One frozen focal figure per sheet, never two competing heroes.

options.label: The Exhibition
options.lineage: white-cube gallery shows and their wall labels
options.thesis: The portfolio is a solo show: projects hang as works with tombstone labels, and you walk the room by scrolling.
options.viewport: The show's title wall: NAVIN set large, the wall text beside it, and Room 1 visible at the edge.
options.risk: Very familiar: minimal gallery portfolios are a common landing spot, so it needs extreme restraint and real typographic finish.

options.label: Type Specimen
options.thesis: The portfolio as a live type specimen; the visitor's input reshapes the letters.
options.viewport: NAVIN at enormous size with a weight slider beneath it, tiny labels around the edge.
options.case: Demonstrates front-end craft directly (holds clarity), but recruiters do not identify with foundry specimens (loses audience identification).
options.risk: Can read as a font demo rather than a person's portfolio.

options.label: VU Meter Bridge
options.thesis: A row of identical meters that move together.
options.viewport: A meter bridge with needles reading skill levels.
options.case: Skill meters would invent levels the product cannot prove; loses both axes.
options.kept: Identical units repeated as the ruler.

options.label: Glaze Shelf
options.thesis: Samples in one shelf row, each with its recipe beside it.
options.viewport: A shelf of glazed cups with recipe cards.
options.case: Craft material unrelated to software; loses both axes.
options.kept: Every sample carries its recipe beside it.

options.label: Alien Understory
options.thesis: Paths light themselves as you approach.
options.viewport: A glowing path through a dark forest.
options.case: Neon-on-dark, against the minimal brief; loses both axes.
options.kept: Destinations announce themselves as you approach.

options.label: Raygun Layout Desk
options.thesis: Columns collide; reading order is earned.
options.case: Deliberate illegibility fails a recruiter skimming in a minute; loses both axes.
options.kept: One loudest fragment sets the entry point.

options.label: Wuxia Hoarding
options.thesis: A frozen figure mid-leap against painted cloud.
options.viewport: A painted figure with vertical title characters.
options.case: Painterly and loud against a minimal brief; loses both axes.
options.kept: One frozen focal figure per frame.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: A clean minimal developer portfolio, executed at full craft.
canonCard.viewport: Large name and one-line intro, a nav top-right, selected work below.
canonCard.risk: Indistinguishable from thousands of other portfolios by design.
